title: The statewide standing order for pharmacist dispensing of emergency contraception
rule_summary: In M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19A, emergency contraception means any drug approved by the federal Food and Drug Administration as a contraceptive method for use after sexual intercourse, whether provided over-the-counter or by prescription. The department shall ensure that a statewide standing order is issued to authorize the dispensing of emergency contraception by a licensed pharmacist, and the statewide standing order shall include, but not be limited to, written, standardized procedures or protocols for the dispensing of emergency contraception by a licensed pharmacist. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, the commissioner, or a physician designated by the commissioner who is registered to distribute or dispense a controlled substance in the course of professional practice pursuant to s. 7, shall issue a statewide standing order that may be used by a licensed pharmacist to dispense emergency contraception under s. 19A. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, a licensed pharmacist may dispense emergency contraception in accordance with that statewide standing order.
exam_relevance: Tests what emergency contraception covers, that the department ensures a statewide standing order is issued, who issues it and what it must include, and that a licensed pharmacist dispenses in accordance with it.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19A(a)-(b), and s. 19A(c), first sentence

common_confusions: Limiting emergency contraception to prescription products when the definition covers drugs provided over-the-counter or by prescription.
Treating issuance of the emergency contraception standing order as discretionary when s. 19A(b) says the commissioner or designated physician shall issue it.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19A on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-14.
